title: Unbroken phase
intro:
Each row of the table is one operator of the renormalised action Sren=S0+δS(1)+ΔSST(1) around H=0, with its coefficients, Feynman rules and the graphs that fix them.

The unbroken phase is the expansion around H=0, with the mass parameter m2 of either sign. Each row of the table is one operator of the renormalised action Sren=S0+δS(1)+ΔSST(1) with definite field content: S0 is the regularised classical action in d=4−2⁢ϵ dimensions (gauge fixing in the Feynman gauge, ghosts, BRST sources and the sterile partners of the fermions included), δS(1) the singular MS-bar counterterm, whose coefficients contain 116π21ϵ and which includes evanescent operators, and ΔSST(1) the finite counterterm that restores the Slavnov–Taylor identity, whose coefficients contain 116π2. The breaking Δ1=𝐬S0 is not part of the action and is listed for its Feynman rule. Every Feynman rule is i times the vertex function V shown, with all momenta incoming.

The operators, coefficients and vertex functions are those of the automation run; the Exposé of an operator shows the one-loop graphs of the Green's functions that fix its coefficients and a card of theory taken from the report.

The operators are the monomials of the report's basis (Table 8), the evanescent operators and the tree-level terms outside that basis. Their coefficients are the exact decomposition of the automation's order store on these operators and agree with the report: the 39 non-zero rα, the 20 renormalisation constants and the 8 evanescent operators.

overview.title: The renormalised action
overview.text: At one loop the renormalised action is the classical action, the singular counterterm (MS-bar poles in ϵ, with d=4−2⁢ϵ) and the finite counterterm that restores the Slavnov–Taylor identity (report Section 5.1). The table splits it into 130 operators with definite field content: 91 with a tree-level coefficient, 61 with a singular coefficient on a non-evanescent operator (continued to d dimensions as in report Section 5.1), 17 parts of the eight evanescent operators, 44 with a finite coefficient, and the 10 parts of the breaking Δ1, which is not part of the action.

overview.text:
The regularised classical action in d=4−2⁢ϵ dimensions (report Section 3.3): the d-dimensional gauge term; for each multiplet f (Q, U, D, L, E) the physical field ψf=PcfΨf with the four-dimensional covariant kinetic term, its sterile partner χf=Pc‾fΨf with a free four-dimensional kinetic term, and the evanescent kinetic term that couples the two; the Higgs doublet; the Yukawa terms with Ou=Q‾H˜PRU.

The evanescent kinetic term is the only part that is not BRST invariant (Section 3.5).

overview.text:
The sum over r runs over G and W. The closed directions 𝒪A(r), 𝒪g(r), 𝒪c(r), 𝒪ψ(f), 𝒪H of Section 3.8.5 are continued to d dimensions (unsplit indices in the bosonic monomials, the barred vertex in the fermion monomials). Equivalently, δSinv(1) is the first-order term of S0 written in bare fields and couplings; the gauge fixing, the sterile partners and the evanescent kinetic term are not renormalised. The 20 constants of the run (MS-bar, Feynman gauge; each includes 116π21ϵ, and δZgs stands for δgsgs) agree with Table 57 of the report:

overview.title: Singular counterterm: evanescent part
overview.text: The sum runs over r = G, W, B. The operators are EA(r)=∫ddx(A‾μa∂ˆ2A‾aμ)2, EH=∫ddx((∂ˆμH)†∂ˆμH), and E˜F(r), E˜H, the barred minus the d-dimensional kinetic invariants (report Eq. (108)). In the Standard Model S(G)=2⁢gs2, S(W)=2⁢g2, S(B)=10⁢g′23 and Y˜=3⁢yu2+3⁢yd2+ye2. E˜F(r) and E˜H are 𝐛d-closed; EA(r) and EH are not.

overview.title: Finite restoring counterterm
overview.text: The unique solution of the restoring condition under the normalisation conditions (N1)–(N4) (report Eq. (497)), in matrix notation: 𝒜μ and 𝛚 in the representation of the multiplet, all fields, indices, derivatives and Dirac matrices four-dimensional. The fermion, source and Higgs terms ℒψST and ℒHST are written out below. In the basis Qα of Table 8, ΔSST(1)=116π2⁢∑αrα⁢Qα with 39 non-zero rα; they are the finite coefficients of the table. There is no ghost term other than the fermion-source term and no Levi-Civita tensor.

overview.title: Finite restoring counterterm: fermion and source terms

math.text: ℒ^{ST}_ψ=-Σ_fψ̅_f γ^μ (C_f 𝒜_μ+1/2 Σ_r∈fν_{fr} 𝒜^{(r)}_μ) ψ_f−1/4 Σ_f(𝑖 R̅_f 𝛚_C ψ_f−𝑖 ψ̅_f 𝛚_C R_f)

overview.text: With 𝛚C=∑r𝛚(r)⁢Cad(r), Cf the Casimir of the multiplet and νfr the Yukawa numbers of Section 4.2.4. Only the physical chirality ψf enters.

overview.title: Finite restoring counterterm: Higgs terms
overview.text: In the Higgs terms 𝒜μ is the gauge matrix on the doublet, with the parts 𝒜(W) and 𝒜(B) of the two factors, and Y˜=3⁢yu2+3⁢yd2+ye2. There is no Higgs-source, (H†H)2 or m2 term.

overview.title: The restored Slavnov–Taylor identity
overview.text: X1 is the finite breaking: the four-dimensional projection of the finite part of the one-loop Green's functions with one insertion of Δ1, a local functional of ghost number 1 (report Eq. (26)). 𝐛 is the linearised Slavnov–Taylor operator of S0 in four dimensions. With this condition the one-loop effective action of Sren satisfies the Slavnov–Taylor identity in four dimensions: 𝒫𝒮(Γ)=0 at one loop for ϵ→0 (report Eq. (22)). X1 has no anomaly component, because the anomaly coefficients Dabc vanish for the fermion content of the Standard Model.

terms.remarks: E˜F(G)=−∫ddx(F‾μνaF‾aμν−FμνaFaμν)4 (report Section 5.1); shown is its four-point part. The relative sign of the unbarred and the barred piece sits in the order of the indices of the structure constants. It is 𝐛d-closed and has one coefficient for all its parts. It arises because the closed fermion loops give barred invariants, which differ from the continued ones by this operator.

The relative sign of the unbarred and the barred piece sits in the order of the indices of the structure constants. It is 𝐛d-closed and has one coefficient for all its parts. It arises because the closed fermion loops give barred invariants, which differ from the continued ones by this operator.

The abelian ghost is free: every ghost and source counterterm of the hypercharge factor vanishes, because δZω(B)=δZA(B) and δZω(B)=−2⁢δZg′. Its finite coefficient is zero by the normalisation condition (N3), which excludes the ghost-sector source monomials of the closed ghost and coupling directions.
